review_notes:
I read the whole file and the AlgHom-level lemmas it builds on in TauCeti/Algebra/TensorProduct/Galois.lean. I also checked the Mathlib simp lemmas it interacts with: `BialgHom.coe_toAlgHom`, and `Bialgebra.TensorProduct.map_tmul`, `map_toAlgHom` and `map_toCoalgHom`.

The file has three simp lemmas: `galoisDescend_toAlgHom`, `one_tmul_galoisDescend` and `map_galoisDescend`.

- `galoisDescend_toAlgHom` is proved by `rfl`. It rewrites toward the AlgHom-level descent, so the AlgHom simp lemmas then apply. This is a sensible direction.
- `BialgHom.one_tmul_galoisDescend` is not redundant with the AlgHom version of the same name. `BialgHom.galoisDescend` is a plain def, so the AlgHom lemma does not match `F.galoisDescend hF a` syntactically. Its right-hand side `F (1 ⊗ₜ a)` is already in the normal form that `coe_toAlgHom` produces.
- `map_galoisDescend` has `Bialgebra.TensorProduct.map (BialgHom.id L L) (F.galoisDescend hF)` as its left-hand side. I found no Mathlib simp lemma that rewrites this subterm first. `map_toAlgHom` only fires under `.toAlgHom`, and `map_tmul` only fires on applied elements.

I found no loop. All rewrites go from the descended map to the original F, and the right-hand sides contain no descent terms. I also found no competing rules and no missing simp lemma that real uses need. The remaining `simpa` calls are small closing steps. I did not find a justified simp-interface defect.
